name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in parallel mode on *all* PRs for two weeks. This exposes false positives without blocking merges, giving us real-world data on its value before committing. The trade-off is temporary noise in PR comments, but it’s safer than rolling it out blindly. After two weeks, we’ll have clear metrics to decide whether to adopt it fully.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent in parallel mode trains the team to ignore *all* automated feedback—not just false positives. The real risk isn’t noise; it’s habituation that erodes trust in *any* automated review, even when it’s correct. A better alternative: run PR-Agent in parallel mode on *new contributors only* for two weeks, then measure whether the false-positive rate justifies expanding. Settle it by tracking merge-blocking vs. non-blocking false positives separately—if the latter dominate, the experiment fails.
